pageTitle: AWS WAF Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) prevention rule group
whatThePageStates: This is the detail page for one AWS Managed Rules rule group, AWSManagedRulesAntiDDoSRuleSet (VendorName AWS, WCU 50). It has four content sections: considerations for use (soft mitigation via silent browser challenge, hard mitigation via block, each tunable to high/medium/low suspicion), the labels the rule group adds (generic AWS WAF token-management labels, then the Anti-DDoS namespace labels), and one 'Anti-DDoS rules listing' table with exactly 3 rules. The only enumeration that is a coverage claim is that rules table: ChallengeAllDuringEvent (Challenge), ChallengeDDoSRequests (Challenge), DDoSRequests (Block), each with its description, permitted action overrides, and the label it emits. The page names no Regions, no protected-resource types, no other AWS services, and it makes no supported/not-supported assertion of any kind - every row is a rule that exists in the rule group.

features.featureName: Anti-DDoS rules listing (rules in the AWSManagedRulesAntiDDoSRuleSet managed rule group)
features.statuses: 3 present, 0 absent, 0 partial; 3+0+0=3. The single markdown table has 5 pipe lines: 1 header ('Rule name | Description'), 1 separator ('--- | ---'), and 3 data rows - ChallengeAllDuringEvent, ChallengeDDoSRequests, DDoSRequests. There is no status column and no Yes/No/Partial vocabulary anywhere on the page. Presence in the table is the only claim: the rule ships in the rule group. The 'Rule action' values inside the description cells (Challenge, Challenge, Block) are default behaviour, not support status, and the override sentences ('You can only override this rule action to Allow or Count', 'AWS WAF only evaluates this rule if you override the action to Count in the prior rule') are configuration constraints, not a Partial state - reading them as Partial would invent a tri-state the page does not have.
features.scope: None. The page states one scope-like qualifier - VendorName AWS, Name AWSManagedRulesAntiDDoSRuleSet, WCU 50, and a note that the content covers only the most recent static version of the rule group - so every row belongs to that single rule group and version. There is no per-Region, per-plan, per-resource-type or per-scan-method second dimension. Availability of the rule group itself (which Regions, which protected resource types, CloudFront vs regional) is not on this page.
features.reasoning: The page enumerates one thing that a reader could count and compare over time: the named rules inside this rule group. That is the unit of claim - a rule either is listed here or it is not. The containing catalogue value 'managedRuleGroup' does not fit as the axis because this page names exactly one rule group; the rule group is the page's subject, not its enumerated axis. The axis name 'managedRuleGroupRule' is NEW - it is not in the supplied vocabulary, and 'ipsRule' would be a bad fit because that term belongs to Network Firewall signature sets, not AWS WAF managed rules. If the wider measurement counts rule groups rather than rules, this page contributes exactly 1 managedRuleGroup value, not 3; the two units must not be mixed.

shouldNotExtract: The label documentation is not coverage. The 'Token labels' subsection describes generic AWS WAF token-management labels shared by every intelligent-threat rule group (client session id, browser fingerprint, the two namespace prefixes awswaf:managed:token: and awswaf:managed:captcha:, and the status names accepted / rejected / rejected:not_solved / rejected:expired / rejected:domain_mismatch / rejected:invalid / absent) - these are output values, not things this rule group supports or does not support. The 'Anti-DDoS labels' subsection lists 6 label names (event-detected, ddos-request, low-suspicion-ddos-request, medium-suspicion-ddos-request, high-suspicion-ddos-request, challengeable-request) plus 3 per-rule labels named inside the table cells - also output values, and counting them would double-count the 3 rules. Also not coverage: the console-experience banner at the top of the page, the repeated 'This documentation covers the most recent static version release' note (it appears twice), the pricing note, the WCU 50 capacity figure (a quota, not a count of anything covered), the two soft/hard mitigation bullets, the high/medium/low sensitivity settings, the cross-links to waf-anti-ddos-advanced, waf-managed-protections and its best-practices page, and the entire 'See also' AI-coding-assistant / Agent Toolkit boilerplate bullet.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page never names a Region, a partition, an availability list, or CloudFront-vs-regional scope. Any per-Region figure attributed to this page is fabricated. SERVICE: nothing beyond the fact that the page is AWS WAF documentation; it mentions Amazon CloudWatch only as the destination for label metrics and the AWS Support Center only as a contact link - neither is a covered service. There is no service enumeration. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing. The page repeatedly says 'protected resource' generically and never lists which resource types (Application Load Balancer, CloudFront distribution, API Gateway, App Runner, Cognito user pool, Verified Access, Amplify) can be protected by this rule group. The only dimension this page supplies is the rule catalogue inside one managed rule group: 3 rules.
trap: The single most likely misparse is harvesting the label bullets as coverage values - the Anti-DDoS labels section alone yields 6 bullet-shaped names and the token labels section another 7 to 9, so a bullet-hungry parser reports 13 to 15 'covered' items for a page whose only enumeration is 3 rules, and the same 3 rules get counted twice because each rule's label is repeated in its table cell. Runners-up: (1) treating the 'Rule action' values or the 'You can only override this rule action to Allow or Count' sentences as a Yes/No/Partial status column, when the page has no status column at all; (2) counting the table's header and separator lines and reporting 5 rows instead of 3; (3) mistaking this single-rule-group detail page for the AWS Managed Rules list page and recording it as 1 managedRuleGroup while a sibling page records the same rule group again, or conversely inflating the rule-group catalogue by 3; (4) reading the WCU 50 figure or the high/medium/low sensitivity levels as a count; (5) scraping the 'See also' Agent Toolkit bullet as content.
